newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears 23.76 billion francs aid for GAN.
newsitem.headline: EU clears 23.76 billion francs aid for GAN.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday cleared a French rescue plan for GAN after France confirmed it would privatise the loss-making firm, the country's fifth largest insurer.

The plan consists of a capital injection of 11 billion francs ($1.77 billion), mainly to cover huge losses recorded by GAN's property unit UIC, and a state guarantee valued at 9.9 billion francs for future losses in restructuring the GAN group. It also includes a 2.86-billion-franc state injection carried out in 1995.
It is the second time in two years that the EU has agreed to bailouts for GAN, bringing the total bill for French taxpayers to 23.76 billion francs.
In return for the new aid, the French government agreed to sell GAN and its banking unit CIC either together or separately, the Commission said in a statement.
GAN will also divest property units UIC and UIS, sell other holdings for a total value of 2.4 billion francs and halve its foreign commercial interests, it said.

It urged the French government to find strong buyers capable of ensuring the long-term viability of the disposed assets, in an apparent hint that it would frown at a sale to other French state-controlled groups.
The French Finance Ministry said the government would bear in mind the best interests of the firms and the state finances when privatising the banking and insurance group.
"The sale of GAN and CIC will be conducted with two concerns in mind, the interests of the companies and their staff and the finances of the state," it said in a statement.
GAN currently holds 93 percent in CIC, also France's fifth largest banking group with a network of 10 regional banks across the country.

The Commission said that before the end of 1998 GAN must have divested CIC and UIC and 2.4-billion francs worth of other holdings. The French government must also begin its search for potential buyers for GAN and CIC as soon as possible and no later than June 30, 1998, it said.

The EU executive, which must approve all government aid plans to salvage ailing industries, said the overall measures, some of which have already been announced by the French group, would ensure the return to profit of GAN, which has lost 35 billion francs since 1992.
"(The Commission) reached the conclusion that the new restructuring measures being undertaken will help GAN to break even or do even better," it said in a statement.
GAN said earlier this month it had started the sale of UIC, which ran up 30 billion francs of losses in three years, the root of GAN's financial problems

The new French government of Socialist leader Lionel Jospin recently endorsed the planned privatisation of GAN and a number of insurance companies have said they were interested in the company, including AGF , Allianz of Germany and Assicurazioni Generali SpA of Italy.
Eureko, a Dutch-based alliance of six European financial services companies with no French presence, also said last week it wanted to take over all of GAN and a maximum of 25 percent of CIC.

GAN currently generates about 25 percent of its revenue abroad, the Commission said. It has operations in Britain, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Germany, Switzerland, Morocco, Canada and the United States. ($1 = 6.20 francs)
